# Best open-ear earbuds for running

I can't open product pages, so the buy links below go to the review pages that list retailers and current prices, except the AeroFit 2, which has a direct store link.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds.** Runner's World ranks them first for audio quality and a comfortable clip-on fit, and they stay put. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. The downsides are 7 hours of battery, an IPX4 rating (so not for heavy rain), and a price that has dropped from $299 to $199. Runner's World also says Bose plans a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.** It has a neckband design, 12 hours of battery, IP55 and physical buttons. WIRED says it is the best for runners who want bass and full awareness of their surroundings, though clarity is a bit lower than Bose. List price is $180, with $125 listed at Best Buy and REI. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200).** It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating. WIRED named it best overall. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Best budget: JLab Flex Open (about $40).** Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to try clip-ons. Sound is less detailed than pricier pairs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Best value hook-style: Soundcore AeroFit 2.** It has IP55, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), and SoundGuys picked it as the best budget open-ear pick. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **Also strong: Nothing Ear (Open).** SoundGuys' top overall open-ear pick and its pick for running, with strong bass and IP54. About $99 at Amazon, down from $149. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**On the AeroFit 2 deal:** Dealectric lists code AFSC20 for $25.99 off a $129.99 store price, which comes to $104. SoundGuys shows it at $79.99 on Amazon (MSRP $99.99). The code may not be the best price, so compare both before buying. Dealectric earns a commission on that link, and the store's checkout has the final word on the code. [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2) · [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**How to choose**
- **Maximum awareness, plus bass:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. Watch for band interference with ponytails and hats.
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open, or wait for the new model.
- **Rain and marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** JLab Flex Open or Soundcore AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs don't isolate sound, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Tell me your budget and whether you wear glasses or hats, and I can narrow it to one pick.
